macro.reasoning: Temperature shows a clear seasonal warming trend from late May (31-34°C) through a cool, wet period in late June/early July (27-30°C) to a recent recovery (28-29°C). The last 10 days show a steady warming trend (+0.7°C) with humidity falling from 77% to 71% and precipitation decreasing. This pattern suggests continued warming toward the seasonal norm of ~31°C. The forecast projects a gradual increase of ~0.3°C/day over the 7-day horizon, consistent with the current recovery trajectory and typical mid-summer warming.

micro.reasoning: Temperature shows a clear warming trend over the last 10 days (28.5→29.3) with decreasing humidity (77→71) and moderate precipitation. The recent pattern suggests continued gradual warming as the region transitions from a cool, wet period to warmer, drier conditions typical of mid-summer.

synthesis.reasoning: Both macro and micro forecasts agree on a steady warming trend of ~0.3°C/day over the next 7 days, driven by the observed recovery from the cool/wet period in early July (27-30°C) toward seasonal norms (~31°C). The macro forecast projects a slightly more conservative endpoint (31.2°C) while the micro forecast extends the recent +0.3°C/day trend to 31.3°C. The combined prediction averages these endpoints and interpolates linearly, reflecting high confidence in the warming trajectory given consistent humidity decline (77%→71%) and decreasing precipitation in the last 10 days. Uncertainty is low for the first 3-4 days (strong trend persistence) but increases slightly toward day 7 as the warming trend may mature near seasonal averages.
